blocks.text: From November 12 to 15, 2026, Paris Photo brings together 246 exhibitors at the Grand Palais, including 199 galleries and 48 publishers, from 38 countries. For its 29th edition, the fair welcomes 80 new participants. Spread across five sectors, it offers an international panorama of the medium, from historical works to the most recent practices.

The Bicentennial of photography is one of the guiding threads of this edition. Rather than a retrospective celebration, Paris Photo offers a reading of the medium that questions its history, its technical developments and its new forms. At the heart of the nave, the Principal sector brings together 152 international galleries. Several galleries specializing in historical photography, including Gilles Peyroulet and Bruno Tartarin, who highlight the origins of the medium. Hans P. Kraus Jr. notably presents works made using the earliest processes by some of the very first practitioners, such as Louis Daguerre, William Henry Fox Talbot, Anna Atkins and Girault de Prangey. Other contemporary projects extend this celebration. Christophe Gaillard presents a solo show of Isabelle Le Minh, whose work explores the history, forms and limits of the medium. Galerie Binome will show a selection of works that test the materiality of photography. A Bicentennial trail connects these various proposals throughout the fair. From the entrance of the Grand Palais, a monumental installation devoted to Thomas Ruff welcomes visitors. Created in collaboration with five galleries – David Zwirner, Konrad Fischer, Mai 36, Lia Rumma, Sprüth Magers the work unfolds as a 36-meter-long retrospective hang tracing more than forty years of creation. A major figure of the Düsseldorf School, Thomas Ruff has explored the possibilities of photography since the 1980s through a wide variety of subjects and techniques, from silver-based images to digital simulations.

The Voices and Digital sectors extend this reflection on the transformations of the medium. Conceived by Francesco Zanot and Zasha Colah, the Voices sector takes Disappearance (La disparition) as its theme. The proposal starts from a paradox: conceived in part to preserve what might disappear, photography celebrates its bicentennial just as its own forms are changing. Curated by Marco de Mutiis, the Digital sector examines how technology is transforming the production and perception of images, while placing these developments within the history of photography.

On the first floor of the Grand Palais, the Émergence sector presents twenty solo projects devoted to a new generation of artists. The Éditions sector brings together 48 publishers from 17 countries. Paris Photo also invites the Centre Pompidou to present Révéler (Reveal), a hanging made from its photography collection. Bringing together about a hundred works by some thirty historical and contemporary artists, the presentation offers a journey through photographic practices from the 20th century to today.

The Elles x Paris Photo trail, which highlights the work of women artists, is entrusted this year to Aldeide Delgado and completes the program alongside the Conversations, the Book Talks, the educational project, the Paris Photo Aperture PhotoBook Awards and more than 400 artist signings. During the week of the fair, partner museums, foundations, institutions and galleries are also presenting photography exhibitions, making of Paris the international meeting place for the medium.
